review_note: Pinned crystalline.tex L1571 compared with proof-masked source and independently examined: The category CRIS(X/S) admits nonempty finite limits, with thickening fibre products and products computed using the compatible divided-power structures; the forgetful functor to the underlying X-scheme data preserves these limits. The nonempty qualifier remains.
statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

Under the global crystalline setup stated above,
The category $\text{CRIS}(X/S)$ has all finite nonempty limits,
in particular products of pairs and fibre products.
The functor the forgetful functor $(U,T,\delta)\mapsto U$ commutes with limits.

statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

Under the global crystalline setup stated above, Let
$$
\xymatrix{
(U_3, T_3, \delta_3) \ar[d] \ar[r] & (U_2, T_2, \delta_2) \ar[d] \\
(U_1, T_1, \delta_1) \ar[r] & (U, T, \delta)
}
$$
be a fibre square in the category of divided power thickenings of
$X$ relative to $(S, \mathcal{I}, \gamma)$. If $T_2 \to T$ is
flat and $U_2 = T_2 \times_T U$, then $T_3 = T_1 \times_T T_2$ (as schemes).

\label{lemma-divided-power-thickening-base-change-flat}
In Situation \ref{situation-global}. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
(U_3, T_3, \delta_3) \ar[d] \ar[r] & (U_2, T_2, \delta_2) \ar[d] \\
(U_1, T_1, \delta_1) \ar[r] & (U, T, \delta)
}
$$
be a fibre square in the category of divided power thickenings of
$X$ relative to $(S, \mathcal{I}, \gamma)$. If $T_2 \to T$ is
flat and $U_2 = T_2 \times_T U$, then $T_3 = T_1 \times_T T_2$ (as schemes).
